answer: Reputation-weighted transaction toll. Each identity pays a toll proportional to its unmet history: new agents pay a high per-action fee that decays as verified activity accumulates, like a river carving its channel wider over time. A marble of attested volume buys lower tolls; an attacker forging N identities pays N times the high initial rate. Faking history requires real settled spend, so each extra plume of fake identity costs the full entry toll in fees.
